correctness.rationale: For all \(n\ge2\) the complete primitive rays are \(v_{p,q}\) with entries −(2n−1),1,2. Their sum is zero, so a Demazure root would have only two nonzero ray pairings \(\pm1\). When \(n\ge3\) two untouched rows of pairings \(2S-(2n+1)a_p-a_q\) force a constant character (hence zero); for \(n=2\) any four distinct ray generators span N_Q. For \(n\ge3\) the two coordinate facet types have n versus \(n(n-1)\) rays; for \(n=2\) their primitive cone indices are 3 versus 8. Thus every fan automorphism preserves lower facets and equals an \(\mathfrak S_{n+1}\) coordinate permutation. The standard Demazure/Sancho complete-toric automorphism theorem then yields \(\operatorname{Aut}(X_n)\cong T_N\rtimes\mathfrak S_{n+1}\) with no missing connected root subgroups. The delivered exact Python checker reconstructs fans and confirms every two-ray deletion is full rank mod1009 through \(n=8\); that finite calculation is corroboration, not the proof of the infinite statement.

value.rationale: Determining the *full* automorphism group, including component group and absence of unipotent roots, is a natural intrinsic stabilizer question for an infinite new family of K-polystable toric Q-Fano varieties. The theorem shows that nondiagonal coordinate permutations give \(\mathfrak S_{n+1}\) symmetries and, in all higher dimensions even where the fan is nonsimplicial, the identity component has no root subgroups. This is geometric information not conveyed by the existing alpha-invariant computation or local singularity class groups, and it has plausible use in K-moduli stabilizers and equivariant geometry; no downstream moduli theorem is asserted.
